new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary word stress is fixed on the first syllable of the word (a Jitotolteco innovation; the Chiapas Zoque dialect chain it split from has penultimate stress). The same sentence appears in Gómez González 2022 §1.5 p. 26, whose phonological sketch transcribes initial primary stress on all ~300 phonetic forms, including 4-5-syllable inflected words.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress in either source; transcriptions mark primary stress only.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Observation from Gómez González 2022 p. 51 ex. 32g-i (not an explicit rule): words carrying the 1sg possessor person marker ʔɨn- are transcribed with stress on the first stem syllable ([ʔɨn.ˈla.ʂu] 'mi lazo', [ʔɨ.ˈna.ma] 'mi jabón'), i.e. person proclitics appear to sit outside the stress domain.
new_statements.domain_note: Stated for 'las palabras' (the word); illustrated with citation-form nouns and with inflected verbs elsewhere in the sketch ([ˈkjotaba] 'se lo inserta', [ˈkun.da.ma] '¡bájense!'). Stressed-syllable position also conditions allophony (ŋ→k, n→t in a stressed syllable before a consonant, items 8-9, pp. 17-18). No phrase-level prosody discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Both sources describe Jitotolteco as spoken in Ejido Cálido and 15 other localities of Jitotol, Simojovel, San Andrés Duraznal and Huitiupán (Chiapas) = Glottolog jito1235 (no ISO code; ELAR files it under zoq). Note ELAR census input maps the deposit to taba1264 'Tabasco Zoque' — that mapping is wrong; the deposit is jito1235. The contrasting penultimate-stress statement in the same sentence refers to the Chiapas Zoque dialect chain (Pantepec/Tecpatán; chia1261 group), and 'zoque sureño' final stress presumably to the Chimalapa (Oaxaca) Zoque languages.

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog (initial, initial stress) and identical wording to the existing statement from Zavala et al. 2024 Tlalocan p. 15 (that paper's item 3 is a verbatim reuse of this sketch's item 3) and to Gomez Gonzalez 2022 sec. 1.5. Adds nothing on secondary stress; the possessor-prefix transcriptions suggest the domain is the stem rather than the prefixed word, which the catalog does not encode.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the first syllable of the word; trisyllables are therefore stressed on the antepenult. Of the 385 stress-marked phonetic forms in the sketch, 356 are word-initial; the 29 others are Pantepec/Tecpatan comparanda (with penultimate/final stress, cited to show the contrast) and possessed nouns with the 1sg possessor prefix ʔɨn-/ʔɨm-/ʔɨŋ-, transcribed with stress on the first syllable of the stem (e.g. /ʔɨn-laʃu/ [ʔɨn.ˈla.ʃu] 'mi lazo', ex. 56i; /ʔɨn-tada/ [ʔɨn.ˈdã.dã] 'mi papa', ex. 104c), which the text does not comment on: the prefix behaves as if outside the stress domain.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned; only primary stress is transcribed ('el acento primario', p. 76 note on representation).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Observed only in transcriptions: forms with the 1sg possessor prefix ʔɨn- carry stress on the stem-initial syllable, not on the prefix (ex. 56g-i, 104a-d, 106); the text gives no rule for this.
new_statements.identity_note: The sketch describes Jitotolteco as spoken in the municipality of Jitotol (Ejido Calido and neighbouring communities in Jitotol, Simojovel, San Andres Duraznal and Huitiupan, Chiapas); no sub-dialect is singled out. Comparative forms labelled PAN and TEC are Pantepec and Tecpatan Zoque (Chiapas Zoque, zoqu1261 area), not Jitotolteco, and are the source of the penultimate-stressed forms in the text.
